1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.f4.strategy: Develops and defends both d4 and e5, so the chain holds. White keeps the space and a solid centre, and Black piles up pressure on d4 and e5 with pieces.
1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.f4.name: French Defence: Steinitz Variation
1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.f4.background: 6.Nf3 is part of the main line of the Steinitz Variation: 5.f4 c5 6.Nf3 Nc6 7.Be3.

1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.f4.strategy: Takes a pawn it cannot keep: Black's knight and bishop both attack c5 and nothing defends it. The capture also gives up the d4 pawn, the base of White's chain, so e5 is left with just the f-pawn behind it. Black regains the pawn and the initiative.
Puts the e5 pawn under double attack before regaining the c5 pawn, which White cannot hold. White must first deal with the threat to the centre, and Black gets the lead in development.
1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.f4.name: French Defence: Steinitz Variation

1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.f4.strategy: Regains the pawn at once with a developing move and keeps the e5 pawn under pressure from the knight. White's chain has lost its d4 base, so e5 is held only by the f-pawn, and Black has an easy game.
Adds a second attacker to d4 and to e5, so both centre pawns are under pressure. Black keeps the tension, and White has to keep its pawn chain protected while it completes its development.
